Define Gene-Centric Non-Coding Regions for One Chromosome and Mask

Source: R/noncoding_regions.R
define_regions_noncoding.Rd

Builds the regions of one gene-centric non-coding mask on one chromosome: one region per gene, whose candidate variants are the records that the mask's annotation links to that gene, wherever they lie on the chromosome. This is how STAARpipeline's gene-centric non-coding analysis forms its sets, computed here once per chromosome and mask instead of once per gene. The regions table carries the candidates as a list column variant_rows that extract_variant_set takes in place of its interval lookup; everything downstream (the filter's QC, type, MAF, MAC and minimum-size tests, LD pruning, collapsing, the tests) is unchanged.

define_regions_noncoding(
  gds,
  chr,
  category,
  filter_spec,
  variant_index = NULL,
  context = NULL,
  rule = c("glow", "staar"),
  gene_list = NULL,
  Annotation_dir = "annotation/info/FunctionalAnnotation",
  Annotation_name_catalog = NULL,
  verbose = 0
)

Arguments

gds

An open SeqVarGDSClass of ONE chromosome, or a path to such a file. A file holding several chromosomes stops with a message.

chr

The chromosome, as the GDS names it (for example 22).

category

One of the eight mask names.

filter_spec

The run's variant_filter: its QC label, pass value and variant type are applied here. Its MAF, MAC and min_variants are NOT applied here; they belong to the per-set extraction, as for every other region type. Its annotation clauses are ignored.

variant_index

A glow_variant_index of the GDS from build_variant_index, or NULL (built here).

context

A context from an earlier call on the same file (the attribute context of a returned table), or NULL (built here). A scan builds one per chromosome and passes it to every mask, so the chromosome-wide vectors are read once.

rule

"glow" (default) or "staar".

gene_list

NULL (the bundled table of the mask's family, on chr) or a character vector of gene names to restrict the links to.

Annotation_dir

Character path prefix for annotations in the GDS.

Annotation_name_catalog

Data frame mapping annotation names to GDS sub-paths. NULL uses the bundled catalog.

verbose

Integer. 1 prints the selection counts.

Value

A data.frame with one row per gene with at least one linked record, in gene-table order: region_id and label (the gene), chr, start and end (the first and last position of the linked records, a descriptive span that is wide for an enhancer far from its gene), n_records (the linked records), category (the mask), gene_rank (the gene's row in its table) and the list column variant_rows (the linked records' row numbers in the chromosome's variant index, unique and increasing). Attributes: context (reusable for the next mask), n_selected_records (the records the mask selected before linkage) and n_linked_records (the (gene, record) links kept).

The eight masks

Every mask starts from the records that pass the filter's QC label and variant type. The masks read five annotation fields of the aGDS, named by their catalog names: GENCODE.Category, GENCODE.Info, GeneHancer, CAGE and DHS; annotate_favor writes all five by default.

MaskGene tableSelectionLinkage fieldTSS window
upstreamprotein-codingcategory has upstreamGENCODE.Infono
downstreamprotein-codingcategory has downstreamGENCODE.Infono
UTRprotein-codingcategory has UTR3 or UTR5GENCODE.Infono
promoter_CAGEprotein-codingCAGE non-emptyGENCODE.Infoyes
promoter_DHSprotein-codingDHS non-emptyGENCODE.Infoyes
enhancer_CAGEprotein-codingCAGE and GeneHancer non-emptyGeneHancerno
enhancer_DHSprotein-codingDHS and GeneHancer non-emptyGeneHancerno
ncRNAncRNA genescategory has ncRNA_exonic or ncRNA_splicingGENCODE.Infono

"Has" means that the ";"-separated token list of the category contains the value. The protein-coding table is the bundled genes_info, the ncRNA table the bundled ncRNA_gene (21,104 names). The two promoter masks keep, among the selected records, those inside the TSS \(\pm\) 3 kb windows of GenomicFeatures::promoters(genes(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene), 3000, 3000), genome-wide, as STAARpipeline does: the window is not tied to the linked gene, so a variant can lie in gene A's window and be linked to gene B by its annotation. The packages TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene, GenomicFeatures, GenomicRanges and IRanges are needed for those two masks only; the aGDS must be on hg38, which the code does not verify.

The linkage rules

Under the default rule = "glow" a record is linked by the meaning of its annotation field, so that FAVOR v1 strings and the FAVOR 2.0 layout written by annotate_favor give the same links wherever the information is present in both. Every balanced parenthesized detail is removed first; ";" separates the gene groups of a multi-category record (one group per category token, in order) and "," the genes of a group; NONE is a sentinel; hyphenated names stay whole.

  • upstream, downstream: the genes of the group at the position of the mask's category token, so an upstream;downstream record joins both masks with its own group in each.

  • UTR: all genes of the UTR groups (a record annotated to two genes' UTRs joins both).

  • promoter_CAGE, promoter_DHS: the first gene of the first group; a NONE first token links to no gene.

  • enhancer_CAGE, enhancer_DHS: the first listed connected gene of the first GeneHancer element; a header without targets links to no gene. Later targets are not used.

  • ncRNA: all genes of all groups, restricted to the ncRNA table.

In the FAVOR 2.0 layout the group boundaries of a two-category record are not serialized, and such a record is then linked to every gene it names under each of its masks. The link is then restricted to the mask's gene table, without fallback to another gene. rule = "staar" reproduces STAARpipeline 0.9.8's literal string operations mask by mask (the whole category string must equal one of the values the function tests, so an upstream;downstream record joins neither of those two masks, while the UTR function accepts UTR5;UTR3 and the ncRNA function ncRNA_exonic;splicing; the UTR text before the first "("; the promoter first token after a split on "(", ",", ";" and "-"; the ncRNA first ";" group with one greedy removal of its parenthesized text and its first three "," tokens) and exists for the validation that enumerates the differences.

See also

noncoding_filter, extract_variant_set, define_regions_gene

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
idx <- build_variant_index("chr22.gds")
spec <- variant_filter(rare_maf_cutoff = 0.01)
up <- define_regions_noncoding("chr22.gds", 22, "upstream", spec, idx)
ctx <- attr(up, "context")                  # reuse for the next mask
enh <- define_regions_noncoding("chr22.gds", 22, "enhancer_DHS", spec, idx,
                                context = ctx)
vset <- extract_variant_set("chr22.gds", up[1, ], spec, variant_index = idx)
} # }
